text:
Maria: Heads up — saw repeated Xid(31) on three us-west nodes after the kernel patch at ~02:12 UTC. Snippets below. Thinking this is a flaky card or driver/kernel interaction, want to speed up attribution so oncall can decide drain vs bake.
Aj: Can you paste the dmesg tail + nvidia-smi -q -x from one of the affected hosts?
Maria: Yup, grabbed from node gpu-usw2-134. Paste below (cleaned IDs):
```
[ 1023.456789] NVRM: Xid (31) GPU at 00000000:3B:00:00: PID 1234: Gpu watchdog: hang detected
[ 1023.456795] NVRM: Xid (31) GPF: GPU has fallen off the bus
[ 1023.458000] nvidia 0000:3b:00.0: bios: NVBios Version 93.27.0
[ 1023.459000] nvlink: pcie link down 0000:3b:00.0
```
Maria: and nvidia-smi -q excerpt:
```
Attached GPUs : 1
Product Name : H100-SXM
Persistence-M: Enabled
ECC Mode : On
Compute Mode : Default
Processes : 0
NVML Xid info : last Xid=31 (Gpu watchdog)
```
InfraBot: Incident note: node gpu-usw2-134 marked Unhealthy by health-agent (Xid threshold=3 in 24h) at 1852109885. Drain task queued. :gear:
Ryan: Do we see ECC counts incrementing in the hw logs or just Xid events? ECC would point to memory faults; Xid31 is more generic. Can you also cat /proc/driver/nvidia/gpus/0000:3B:00.0/information and /proc/driver/nvidia/gpus/0000:3B:00.0/memoryTelemetry?
Maria: Checked - ECC correctable count is low, not ramping. journalctl shows repeated kernel messages right before Xid 31: 
```
Mar 21 02:12:33 gpu-usw2-134 kernel: nvidia 0000:3b:00.0: GPU assertion failed: 0x4a
Mar 21 02:12:33 gpu-usw2-134 kernel: nvlink error: lane 2 training timed out
Mar 21 02:12:33 gpu-usw2-134 kernel: NVRM: Xid (31) at 0x7f3b2d
```
Leah: Sounds like link training / NVLink flakiness rather than DRAM ECC. Could be firmware mismatch or power capping regression after the kernel bump. Two asks: (1) get full dmesg from boot to Xid (2) nvml logs with timestamped driver messages. I can land a small loghook to grab those automatically on next Xid.
Devon: Quick ops question — what's our current auto-replace policy? Do we rotate after 3 Xid events in 24h or wait for manual triage? Last I remember policy was 5 events in 7d -> replace, but health-agent has a lower drain threshold for user safety.
Aj: Correct: health-agent auto-drain threshold is conservative (3 in 24h) to avoid noisy retries. Replacement (RMA/replace) requires 5 confirmed hardware faults in 7d. But we should tune if kernel updates spike false positives.
Aj: For faster triage we should parse both Xid and NVLink keywords. Proposal for a single-line grep + awk we can add to loghook:
```sh
journalctl -k -b --no-pager | egrep -i "Xid|nvlink|gpu watchdog|GPU has fallen off the bus" | tail -n 200
journalctl -u nvidia-persistenced --since "-1h" --no-pager
nvidia-smi --query-gpu=timestamp,index,utilization.gpu,temperature.gpu,memory.total,memory.free --format=csv -l 1 -f /tmp/gpu-telemetry.csv & sleep 5; pkill -f "nvidia-smi"
```
Ryan: Nice. Also add a small parser to normalize Xid codes to a short label (Xid31_watchdog, Xid13_illegal, ecc_uncorrectable). That'll make dashboards and alerts less noisy.
Maria: I'll open a quick PR to add the hook to health-agent: collect 200 lines of dmesg + last 500 journald kernel lines + nvml snapshot on Xid event and attach to the node ticket. Will include the grep from Aj and the Xid->label mapping.
Leah: When you do, include NVLink lane state from `nvidia-smi -q -d LINK` and PCIe errors from `dmesg | grep -i pcie` — those helped in the last incident.
Devon: Ops action: for this set of nodes let's keep them drained and run burn-in (memtest + nvlink stress) while replacement is queued. If tests fail, RMA. If clean, reintroduce after kernel rollback validation.
Maria: Plan acknowledged. I'll create tickets for the three nodes, attach the collected snippets, and post PR link. Oncall: leave them drained for now. :white_check_mark:
Aj: Thanks — please ping when PR is up and I'll add regex to alert pipeline to correlate NVLink + Xid counts across region.
Maria: PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/health-agent/pull/412 (WIP) — adds Xid snapshot hook and nvlink capture. I'll post updates here.
InfraBot: Reminder: automated drain will complete in ~10m unless manually aborted.
